chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:
I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about ghusl (ritual bath) for janabah (major ritual impurity),

So he said: "Wash your right hand from the elbows to your fingers, and urinate if you are able to urinate. Then put your hand into the vessel, then wash whatever of it has affected you. Then pour water over your head and your body, and there is no wudu (ablution) in it."

key_terms.الْإِنَاءِ: the vessel containing water used for purification
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمِرْفَقَيْنِ: the elbows, marking the upper point from which the hand is washed
key_terms.جَسَدِكَ: your body, which must be washed in ghusl
key_terms.رَأْسِكَ: your head, over which water is poured in ghusl
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: ritual ablution, which the hadith states is not separately required here

ai.seo_question: What is the method of ghusl al-janabah, and is separate wudu required in it?
ai.summary: This hadith states the procedure for ghusl al-janabah, beginning with washing the right hand, urinating if possible, and then pouring water over the head and body. It also indicates that a separate wudu (ablution) is not required within this ghusl.
